_meta.title: IGVC AutoNav Challenge — Prior Winners & Public Code
_meta.scope: Top-3 finishers in the AutoNav Challenge (formerly Auto-Nav) at the Intelligent Ground Vehicle Competition, 2018-2025.
notes: 2020 was cancelled due to COVID-19 — no results PDF exists between r2019 and r2021.
Placements verified against official IGVC scoresheet PDFs; design reports linked under http://www.igvc.org/design/<year>/<team-number>.pdf.

Sources for 2021 2nd-place disagree: official scoresheet shows Cedarville 'Alpha Bee' 213ft beating BJU; BJU news release also claims '2nd at 2021 IGVC' — likely referring to Self-Drive or a sub-award. We use the AutoNav scoresheet.
Every GitHub URL was verified to load by the research agents.
Project MANAS (Manipal) and most Indian/Millersville/BJU/NMIMS teams keep their code private — `github` is null where no public repo exists.

winners.description: Modified Jazzy electric wheelchair chassis. SJ4000 action camera + Hokuyo LMS (270deg, 30m) + Hemisphere A21 GPS + Maretron solid-state compass. Parallax Propeller 8-core MCU + Raspberry Pi 3B+, software in LabVIEW (later cross-compiled to ROS C/C++). Planning on 80x80 weighted-node grid with Dijkstra/A*/JumpPointSearch baseline plus a custom 'Knight-Star' heuristic. 412 ft on course — nearly 2x the next team. Tied for Grand Award (Lescoe Cup).

Four-wheel-steer aluminum-6061 platform with independent planetary steering + brushless hub drive (point-rotation steering). Logitech c930e webcam (OpenCV HSV lane pipeline) + RPLiDAR A1 + Pixhawk 4 GPS/IMU. Custom PCB drives Teensy 3.6 + motor controllers + wireless e-stop. ROS Kinetic on i7 laptop. BreezySLAM particle filter -> 100x100 grayscale costmap -> Dijkstra variant with Manhattan straight-ahead bias. 260 ft. Rookie of the Year.

Teakwood truss chassis (vibration damping), brushed DC + Roboteq MDC2230. VectorNav VN-200 INS + Hokuyo UTM-30LX + PointGrey BFLY-23S6 + 2000-CPR encoders. ROS stack: IPM -> CUDA SLIC superpixels -> RANSAC parabola lanes; Hough Transform for potholes. Dual EKF (odom + map), gmapping, navfn (A*) global + TEB local, FSM switching between Lane and Waypoint nav modes.

Same AWS chassis as 2018 with major software/electronics rework. Added BreezySLAM, custom PCB, hot-swap DeWalt 20V packs. Single Logitech c930e + OpenCV HSV pipeline; LiDAR-camera fusion to remove false lines from elevated barrels. Dijkstra variant on 100x100 dilated costmap with Manhattan straight-ahead weighting. ~0.4 s end-to-end latency at 1.5 mph. 239 ft — largest 1st-vs-2nd gap of any year studied.
Successor to Eklavya 6.0. Same general stack (Roboteq MDC2230, VectorNav, Hokuyo UTM-30LX, gmapping + navfn + TEB). 86 ft.
ROS-based stack with separate planning_control and localization_mapping modules; deep-learning lane segmentation. 77 ft. Also 2nd in Grand Award (Lescoe Trophy).
No 2020 IGVC was held. 28th IGVC was rescheduled to June 2021.

First year competing. Wedge aluminum T-slot chassis, Kinect 2 RGB+D, 2D LiDAR over drive axle, IMU + u-blox GPS, ODROID. Custom STM32 PCBs on CAN bus (motor, GPS, lights, LoRa e-stop). ROS Noetic. U-Net CNN (TensorFlow) for lane detection on hand-labeled chalk imagery, fused with 2D LiDAR. EKF localization with dynamic landmark insertion. D* Lite planner + pure pursuit. Custom Unity simulator publishing same ROS topics. 221 ft, Rookie of the Year, Grand Award 2nd.

Senior design team. Welded steel-tubing frame, Jetson Nano, Intel RealSense D435 + two VL53L0X ToF + QMC5883L compass + ZED-F9P RTK + MDDS30 Cytron. ROS with one node per device + 4-state FSM (Line Following / GPS Nav / Obstacle Avoidance from line / Obstacle Avoidance from GPS). Probabilistic Hough on RealSense RGB; ToF wall-follow around obstacles. NO SLAM, NO global planner — purely reactive. 213 ft, 1.8 mph cruise.

Rewrote DAISI LabVIEW stack to Python ROS. Carbon-fiber + Nomex sandwich chassis in IP65 Pelican. Velodyne VLP-16 Puck Hi-Res + VectorNav VN-300 dual-antenna GNSS-INS + LI-JEVA-IMX424 GMSL2 ADAS camera (3849x1929, 120deg FOV). Jetson TX2. Lane pipeline: downsample 3849x1929 -> 160x120 grayscale, split L/R, Hough per half, dominant-line vote. Path priority: LiDAR -> camera -> GPS waypoints. Polynomial interpolation between waypoints. 158 ft. Grand Award (Lescoe Cup) 2021 + 1st in Design.

525 ft course completed in 5:05. Ubuntu 20.04 on HP ProDesk i5/16GB with a 'mesh of ROS Noetic and Galactic' (Python primary). Intel RealSense for lane + pothole (HSV + Hough circles), Slamtec RPLIDAR A2 M8, Emlid Reach RS+ RTK, optical shaft encoders, Teensy 4.0. Behavioral FSM — no SLAM, no global map. Key trick: paint detected potholes onto the 2D LiDAR scan so a single obstacle-avoidance routine handles barrels, sawhorses AND potholes.

5:11. Continuation of 2021 Aluminum Whale stack — ROS Noetic, same CAN-bus + custom STM32 PCB approach, same U-Net + LiDAR + EKF + D* Lite + pure pursuit. Planner compute (~150 ms/cycle) became the limiter and was rewritten for 2023.

winners.university: SVKM's Mukesh Patel School of Tech (Mumbai)
winners.description: Limited English-language technical info. Listed on the official 2022 design-report index.

2:19 — fastest run of any year studied. Major rewrite to ROS2 Humble on Ubuntu 22.04 (Intel NUC). Sensors: webcam on a tall PVC pole, Emlid Reach RTK, VectorNav IMU. NO LiDAR, NO depth camera — pure OpenCV HSV obstacle detection, with 3x ultrasonic on custom CAN-bus PCB as firmware-level redundancy. Particle filter (GPS + encoders + IMU). Novel tangent-based path planner modelling obstacles as circles (~10 ms vs 150 ms grid-D* of 2022) — 'Smelly Algorithm' goal selection (A* with multi-bias). Pure pursuit. 'CON-bus' CAN protocol for live HSV/PID retuning without reflash.

4:20. Pride Mobility Quantum 614 wheelchair base. NOT a ROS robot — distributed Teensy 3.2 per subsystem, no PC. Two SICK LMS111-10100 industrial 2D LiDARs front-left/right at 45deg using SICK's onboard zone programming (6 trapezoidal zones -> digital pins), SICK TiM881P rear LiDAR for collision during turns, four OpenMV H7 smart cameras for lanes + potholes. GT-U7 GPS + GY-273 mag + Teensy for waypoints. VEXpro Jaguar motor controllers. Custom GUI on SICK AppStudio for live zone tuning.
Did not complete full course — placed by distance traveled (416 ft).

3:24. Six-wheel drop-center diff-drive (2x NEO via REV 10.7:1 gearboxes, SPARK MAX). 2x Logitech C920x USB webcams in PORTRAIT orientation (480x640 @ 8 fps), VectorNav VN-200, wheel encoders. NO LiDAR. Intel NUC, ROS2 Humble (Ubuntu 22.04). Pipeline: box blur -> HSV threshold OR U-Net CNN -> ROD mask -> perspective transform -> 80x80 occupancy grid -> dilation. Particle filter (GPS + encoders). A* planner + pure-pursuit + backup recovery. State machine: autonomous/manual/disabled/shutdown x competition/practice/sim. Custom Molex CAN hub + LoRa wireless e-stop. Largely C++ with Python tooling + custom web GUI.

395 ft (DNF). Industrial wheelchair-base build, multiple SICK LIDARs across iterations, drive-by-wire kit, 80/20 aluminum frame. Distributed control (still no ROS). Speed was their explicit weakness; drove them toward full PLC architecture in 2025.

250 ft. 3-wheel diff-drive (2 driven front + 1 rear caster), 30x30 mm aluminum extrusion + stainless underbody. ZED 2 stereo (sponsored), GPS, no LiDAR (cost choice). Intel NUC. YOLOv8n + Canny edge for lanes — vision-only. Multi-stage E-stop. Android remote with custom heartbeat protocol.

2:20 — fastest completion of either year. Holonomic swerve drive — 4 custom modules, 8 NEO motors (4 drive + 4 steer), REV MAXPlanetary 15:1, SPARK MAX in mixed pos/vel PID on separate CAN buses. 4x SVPRO AR0234 global-shutter USB cameras (one per face, 360deg vision), VectorNav VN-200, ultrasonics. NO LiDAR. Intel NUC, ROS2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04. Per-camera OpenCV pipeline (box blur -> HSV w/ run-start auto-calibration -> ROD -> rotation -> perspective -> 4-way image combination). Navigation is a 2D raycast heuristic (NOT a planner — rays weighted by direction-of-travel and next GPS waypoint; reimplemented in C++ from prior year's A*-in-Python for latency). Particle-filter localization. Custom CONBus protocol, web ROS GUI for live tuning. Single 6-pin Molex carries 12V + CAN + e-stop. Cost ~$5,400.

2:57 (completed course). Fully industrial PLC architecture — Phoenix Contact AXL F 2152 PLC (programmed in PLCNext Engineer), Phoenix Contact Industrial PC running Python + OpenCV on 2x Logitech webcams, SICK NAV310 LiDAR (TCP 2112), QMC5883L compass, NEO-6M GPS, 4x SEW Eurodrive Movimot ELV (Profinet bus). 48V from 2x 24V Dakota Lithium series, sealed Saginaw cabinet. No ROS.

3:02 (completed). Centered diff-drive on 30 mm aluminum T-slot + carbon fiber, passive central-pivot suspension w/ TPU damping. Ouster OS-1 3D LiDAR (used for obstacle detection AND Direct LiDAR Odometry / DLO), ZED 2i stereo, Hiwonder 10-axis IMU @ 200 Hz, Hiwonder GPS (<1 m). ASUS TUF A15 (Ryzen 7 + RTX 4050). Rhino 24V BDC + Cytron MDDS30. Custom STM32G491 drive controller + STM32F401 comms module — all firmware in Rust (memory-safety). USB-CDC + RS-485 + CAN-FD + nRF24L01 wireless e-stop. ROS with quadtree hierarchical occupancy grid, polygonal-FOV depth mapping (mask RGB -> use depth corners as polygon -> iterate only points in polygon), HSV + polynomial-fit lanes. Dynamic ZED-camera height adjustment via lead screw + stepper (350 mm travel) to retune FOV per challenge. ~$7,500 total.

sensor_convergence: Top finishers in 2024 + 2025 (OU, NMIMS, Millersville on the PLC side) almost universally skip Velodyne-class spinning 3D LiDARs.
OU has won 2021/2023/2024/2025 with NO LiDAR — pure camera-based perception.
Only 2025-3rd (Manipal) used a modern 3D LiDAR, and primarily for odometry (DLO), not just costmaps.
Global-shutter USB cameras dominate (SVPRO AR0234 on OU 2025); ZED 2/2i used by Manipal + NMIMS; Logitech webcams used by Millersville + Boise State.
VectorNav VN-200 dominates the US ROS stacks; Xsens MTi-680G + NTRIP RTK (the user's choice) is heavier-spec than what any winner used.
software_stack: ROS2 is now the dominant winner stack: OU 2024 = Humble, OU 2025 = Jazzy, Hosei = Humble, Manipal = generic ROS.
Nav2 is conspicuously absent from winners. OU explicitly REPLACED their A* planner with a 2D raycast heuristic in C++ for latency.
Lane detection: HSV thresholding + simple morphology beats semantic segmentation among winners. U-Net used to catch black barrels that HSV misses.
Live config tuning over CAN ('CON-bus' / 'CONBus') is a Sooner staple — HSV thresholds + PID retunable without reflash.
reactive_vs_slam: 1st-place 2022 (Cedarville Delta Bee) was a pure FSM with no SLAM and no global planner.
Winning courses 2021-2025 trend faster: Aluminum Whale ~5 min -> Delta Bee 5:05 -> Weeb Wagon 2:19 -> Danger Zone 3:24 -> Twistopher 2:20.
Simpler, more reactive software consistently beats heavier SLAM stacks at IGVC's scale (~525 ft course).
drivetrain: OU went swerve in 2025 — speed advantage 2:20 vs 2:57 over Millersville.
Differential-drive (incl. the user's AndyMark Raptor) is still common (Hosei, Manipal, Millersville).

top_picks_for_user_stack.why: Direct ROS2 Humble + Ubuntu 22.04 match to IGVC_ROS2. 2024 1st-place winning code, full Sooner stack, 78% C++. Best one-to-one comparison for your perception + planner.
Single closest hardware match — ROS2 Humble + Nav2 MPPI, ZED 2i + RealSense, Jetson AGX Orin deployment, CAN motor controllers, NVBlox voxel mapping. Actively developed.
First ROS2 Humble Sooner winner. Their 'Weeb Wagon' 2:19 course completion is the fastest run on record. Read for the state-machine + tangent-planner + CON-bus live-tuning patterns.
Hosei University. Most-starred (15) and most-mature ROS2 Humble IGVC stack publicly available. Cartographer + slam_toolbox + Nav2 + multi-sensor drivers.
UMich UMARV ZED-camera BEV/HSV occupancy-grid pipeline mirrors your avros_perception HSV pipeline almost feature-for-feature.
Gold-standard algorithmic reference (93 stars, ROS1, archived). Line detector + nav stack + Gazebo IGVC course — the most-studied public IGVC codebase.
50-star Cartographer 2D/3D SLAM + robot_localization fusion + img-to-laser/img-to-pcloud — best public reference for the sensor-fusion side.
Closest hardware list match for ROS2 Humble — robot_localization, Nav2 bringup, GPS, TF2, Gazebo sim with ros2_control, NMEA + MAVRos. Actively developed.
